content: 1. Certain drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the likelihood of severe side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. 2. Maintain a comprehensive list of all products you use, including prescription drugs, over-the-counter medications, and herbal supplements, and share this list with your doctor and pharmacist. 3. Lamivudine is pharmacologically similar to emtricitabine and should not be taken concurrently with this medication. 4. Carefully review the labels of all your HIV medications to ensure they do not contain the same active ingredients as this product. 5. In the event of an overdose, if the individual exhibits serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, immediately call 911. Otherwise, contact a poison control center without delay. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. 6. Laboratory and medical tests, such as liver function tests, viral load assessments, T-cell counts, and hepatitis B virus testing, should be conducted prior to initiating this medication and periodically during treatment. 7. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is close to the time of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. 8. Store this medication in its original container. Capsules should be kept at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store them in the bathroom. 9. The oral solution should be stored in the refrigerator and must not be frozen. If necessary, it can be stored at room temperature but must be discarded after three months. 10. Do not dispose of medications by flushing them down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. 11. This information was last revised in September 2024. 12. This document provides a summary and does not include all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific situation. 13. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your individual health needs. 14. Common side effects may include headache, diarrhea, difficulty sleeping, or darkening of the skin on the palms of the hands and soles of the feet. 15. This medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of potential side effects. 16. As your immune system strengthens, it may begin to combat pre-existing infections, potentially causing symptoms of these infections to reappear. 17. In some cases, an overactive immune response may occur, which can happen shortly after starting HIV treatment or even months later. 18. Rarely, this medication may cause severe, potentially fatal liver and blood problems, such as lactic acidosis. 19. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare but possible. 20. This is not an exhaustive list of potential side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for similar guidance. 21. Before taking emtricitabine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. 22. If you are pregnant, inform your doctor before using this medication. Treatment can reduce the risk of transmitting HIV to your baby. 23. This medication passes into breast milk but is unlikely to harm a nursing infant. 24. Drug interactions may alter the way your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. 25. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. 26. Lamivudine is similar to emtricitabine and should not be taken with this medication. 27. Check the labels on all your HIV medications to ensure they do not contain the same ingredients as this product. 28. In the event of an overdose, if someone has serious symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call 911. Otherwise, contact a poison control center immediately. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. 29. Laboratory and/or medical tests (such as liver tests, viral load, T-cell counts, and tests for hepatitis B virus) should be performed before starting this medication and while you are taking it. 30. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose. Take your next dose at the regular time. 31. Store this medication in the original container. Capsules should be stored at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store them in the bathroom. 32. The oral solution should be stored in the refrigerator and not frozen. If stored at room temperature, discard it after three months. 33. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. 34.
